A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Flavors of Margin. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original teacher–student and MNIST experiments measuring margins, losses, and generalization under several optimizers, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The steepest-descent/flow procedures, network models, and losses are unchanged. Describing sign gradient descent as normalized steepest descent clarifies the existing relationship without establishing an algorithm or implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate sparse Gaussian teacher–student classification and MNIST digit-pair classification, including the appendix experiment on digits 2 and 7. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GD, CD, and SD in teacher–student experiments; GD, SD, and Adam variants in the Adam experiments; and GD, Adam, and Shampoo in the spectral-margin comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same sample counts, architectures, learning rates, initialization scales, losses, training budgets, and stopping procedures. Moving experimental details and figures does not alter the protocols.

E4.justification: The initialization-scale analysis, switching from GD to CD or SD after separation, Adam precision/momentum comparisons, and additional digit-pair experiment are retained. No empirical ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 seeds for the teacher–student experiment and three seeds for Figure 2, with unchanged averaging, plotted uncertainty, and descriptions of seed-dependent sampling and initialization.

E6.justification: The empirical plots and reported findings are unchanged. Figures 1–3 match across versions, and v2 Figures 5–6 correspond to v3 Figures 4–5 with the same results; the removed v2 Figure 4 is a conceptual illustration.

T1.justification: Theorem A.16 receives a substantially different proof: v2's approximate-iterate argument is replaced by a direct limit-point construction using convergent loss subgradients and bounded multipliers. Appendix B retains the Bregman bound, incorporates the existing complementarity estimate, and adds Proposition B.7, Corollary B.8, and Remark B.9 on finite-time guarantees for smooth squared norms. The general proximity-measure optimization in v2 Appendix B.1 is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of increasing algorithm-dependent margins and directional convergence to KKT points for arbitrary norms, together with connections to Adam and Shampoo. The proof changes support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 now explicitly distinguishes arbitrary-norm asymptotic stationarity from finite-time approximate-KKT guarantees requiring smooth squared norms. It also clarifies that normalized limit points are proportional to KKT points. The empirical interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D preserves the implementation framework, hyperparameters, sampling details, initialization rules, early stopping, and plotting conventions. The normalization explanation in Appendix C.1 restates the existing sign-gradient relationship rather than disclosing a different implementation.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but Section 3.2 revises the technical positioning: it explicitly contrasts the direct limit-point proof with the approximate-KKT sequence approach of Lyu and Li and the earlier ICLR version.

P1.justification: Targeted rewriting updates the proof overview, reorganizes parts of Appendices A and B, clarifies normalization terminology, and changes author and acknowledgment text. The main section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2's conceptual Bregman-proximity illustration, Figure 4, is removed. The retained appendix plots are renumbered, and the additional MNIST plot moves to a separate page. Main empirical figures retain their visual design.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses a central proof gap: v2 Equation (61) assumes convergence of selected norm subgradients from membership in the limiting subdifferential, which is insufficient for nonsmooth norms. The revised Theorem A.16 instead uses closed-graph subsequence arguments and bounded multipliers, substantially strengthening support for the paper's arbitrary-norm claim. The finite-time limitations are also clearer. New Equation (79) appears to omit a square in its strong-convexity bound, but this local auxiliary defect does not outweigh the repair to the central proof.
